tldr: Look up! Used for pointing up, emphasis, or the 'above' attention cue.

seoTitle: 👆 Pointing Up Emoji Meaning - What Does 👆 Really Mean?
seoDescription: Learn what the Pointing Up emoji 👆 really means in modern texting. 'Look above' CTA, emphasis, and how to use it without sounding condescending.

longForm.overview:
👆 is the emoji of 'look up' - a hand with the index finger pointing upward, the universal 'above' or 'see the thing above' cue. Where 👉 says 'look this way' and 👇 says 'look down,' 👆 captures the moment when the sender wants to direct attention to something earlier in the conversation, the caption above, or the previous post. The upward cue borrows from physical pointing gestures and old hyperlink-style references, which is exactly why the emoji reads as 'read the thing before this.'

In real-world usage 👆 lives in the spaces where the sender wants to direct attention to a previous message. A creator sends it on an Instagram story ('full blog above 👆'). A friend sends it on a 'see my last message' reminder. A colleague sends it on a 'look at the previous Slack thread' reply. The upward cue is what makes the emoji feel like a hyperlink in emoji form - it is rarely used literally.

What separates 👆 from the rest of the pointing family is the specificity of direction. The emoji says 'up,' which on left-to-right reading audiences reads as 'before this' or 'earlier.' That is why it pairs so naturally with continuation CTAs, story references, and 'read above' emphasis where the upward cue becomes the entire message.
longForm.howPeopleUseIt:
👆 shows up as a story CTA ('full post above 👆'), the punctuation on a 'see the previous message' reminder ('forgot to mention 👆'), and the softener on a 'look at the previous thread' emphasis. It pairs naturally with sentences that direct attention - 'check above,' 'read this,' 'see prior context' - and sits beautifully on link continuations, story references, and emphasis chains.

In group chats 👆 anchors 'look at the message above' cues, continuation CTAs, and emphatic replies where the upward cue signals 'see prior context.' On Instagram it gravitates toward story continuation CTAs and caption emphasis. On TikTok it lands in 'read the comments above' jokes and 'look at the previous video' captions.

The emoji also works in work contexts. A 'see the thread above 👆' Slack message uses 👆 to direct attention to the prior conversation, which is the cleanest way to signal 'look here.' Across all of these surfaces the rule is the same: the more 'look above' the moment, the more natural 👆 feels.
longForm.whenNotToUse:
Skip 👆 in sympathy, condolence, or break-up contexts. The directional cue is the wrong tone for any conversation where the moment is somber. A quiet ❤️ or a sentence that acknowledges the moment is a better fit.

Avoid 👆 in work contexts where the pointing cue could be read as singling out a coworker. A 'thanks for the help 👆' reply that is meant as sarcasm can land as a complaint. Pair with a clear sentence or use 👍, 🙌, or no emoji for work appreciation.

Skip 👆 when aiming the cue at a person. Pointing 👆 at someone in a complaint ('you 👆 are wrong') reads as confrontational. Pair with a sentence or use a softer emoji when the moment is critical of a specific person.
longForm.howToReply:
If someone sends 👆, the cleanest mirror is another 👆, a sentence that follows the direction, or a clear acknowledgment of the CTA. If you want to escalate the directional cue, follow with a sentence that names what you are pointing at: 'I see the thread above 👆.' If the upward cue feels like an attack, reply with a sentence that addresses the direction ('I hear you, here is my side') rather than another pointing finger that doubles the tension.

When 👆 lands as a 'look above' CTA, mirror with a sentence that acknowledges the prior message. When it arrives as a 'see the previous post' reminder, mirror with a sentence that confirms the reference rather than another pointing finger that doubles the emphasis.

faqs.question: What does 👆 mean in a text?
faqs.answer: In a text 👆 means 'look up' or 'see the thing above' - it is the directional cue used to point at a previous message, the caption above, or the prior post. The emoji is rarely used literally; it almost always functions as a hyperlink in emoji form.

faqs.question: What does 👆 mean from a guy?
faqs.answer: From a guy, 👆 usually signals a directional cue - a CTA to a prior message, an emphasis on a previous point, or a 'see above' reminder. The pointing emoji is rarely used literally; it is almost always a directional shortcut.

faqs.question: Is 👆 passive-aggressive?
faqs.answer: It can be. Pointing 👆 at a coworker in a complaint ('you 👆') reads as confrontational. In a CTA context ('see above 👆') the upward cue is helpful; aimed at a specific person it can land as a passive-aggressive callout.

faqs.question: What is the difference between 👆 and 👇?
faqs.answer: 👆 is the pointing-up emoji - the cue is 'look above' or 'see prior context.' 👇 is the pointing-down emoji - the cue is 'look below' or 'see what follows.' Use 👆 when referencing something earlier; use 👇 when directing attention to what comes next.
